title: Hairpin lace — making the loop strip
subtitle: A crochet hook and a fork frame produce a strip of equal loops on both sides
excerpt: Hairpin lace uses a U-shaped frame (the hairpin or staple) to hold yarn while a crochet hook makes a central chain and turns the frame to create matching loops on each side. The result is a long strip of equal loops — raw material for hairpin lace fabric. This tutorial covers making the strip.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — hairpin (pin) crochet. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 2 (1887) — hairpin lace strip construction.

glossaryTerms.definition: A U-shaped two-prong frame used in hairpin lace. The frame is turned with each stitch to wrap the yarn around its prongs as loops. The width between the prongs sets the loop width. Also called a hairpin staple or hairpin lace loom.
The long strip of equal loops produced by working hairpin lace on a hairpin frame. Each side of the strip has the same number of loops. Strips are joined to make fabric or edging.

content.text: as a tension device. The frame is turned after each stitch, wrapping the yarn around its prongs to build matching loops on each side. A crochet hook works a central spine of dc between the prongs. The
can be any length and is then joined into fabric in a separate pass.
Make a slip knot. Place it on the left prong of the frame. Centre the slip knot between the prongs at the base bar.
Bring the yarn around the right prong from back to front. The yarn crosses between the prongs.
Insert the hook through the loop on the left prong from right to left. Yarn over, draw up a loop, yarn over, pull through both — one dc made at the centre.
Turn the frame 180 degrees (away from you). The yarn wraps around the new left prong automatically.
Insert the hook into the front loop of the left-prong loop. Yarn over, pull up a loop, yarn over, pull through both — one dc.
Repeat: turn frame, dc in front loop. Each turn adds one loop to each side of the frame.

items.cause: Yarn not wrapped consistently around the prong before turning, or turning in different directions
items.fix: Always turn the frame the same direction (away from you is standard). The yarn should wrap the prong cleanly each time — if the wrap is loose before turning, adjust before proceeding.

content.text: The Hairpin braid join tutorial covers attaching strips together into fabric by braiding groups of loops. For a narrower strip with tighter loops, use a smaller frame width.
